analysis:
Both changed files are newly added Swift test files under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/DarkbloomClusterRuntimeTests/. They test Gemma 4 tensor-parallel behavior on synthetic checkpoints and in-process rank pairs. I found no production code, network or WebSocket handling, key custody, attestation, authorization, or prefix-cache storage change in the visible content, so no TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 or T-041 behavior is altered here.

Security-relevant observations:
- Synthetic checkpoints are written to FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory under a UUID path and removed with defer. They contain only synthetic weights and no consumer data (A-001) or credentials.
- Tests exercise refusal paths: verifiedShardEntriesCutEveryTextTensorExactly rejects wrong-shape, vision, unknown and duplicate tensors, and loadAgreementBindsTermsPolicySelectionLanesAndStorage requires differing fingerprints. These tests support integrity of the verified-load and load-agreement paths but make no claim about production enforcement.
- The tests reference prefix-cache agreement fields (prefixCache, kvQuantization) only as load-agreement inputs. They do not touch SSD tier encryption, HMAC tags, TTL, or salt scoping.
- Test-only constructs (@unchecked Sendable Box, LaneHost) are confined to the test target.

Gemma4TensorParallelTests.swift (unit d7cfeedc1744a17f:0) was supplied only as metadata plus a truncated patch excerpt (header-fixture reading and registered tensor loading), so its body is not fully reviewed. It appears to be test-only, reading fixture JSON headers from the repo. Remaining question for integration: production implementations of Gemma4TensorParallel* (outside this batch) should be reviewed for the rank load-agreement and collective-reduction trust assumptions. Nothing in these tests changes that.
